newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up in lethargic trading.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up in lethargic trading.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed in lethargic trade on Thursday with traders forecasting a slip in prices in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 21 issues rose by 0.32 percent to 180.96 on $7.22 million in volume.
"The market is fluctuating around the same level on Russian brokers' speculations," said Oleg Tatkov, a trader from Renaissance-Capital.
Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt, said prices would slip by about one to three percent in the next few days because of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
"There are not enough orders for a sharp rise, but enough to keep the market at current levels," Tatkov said. "I do not know what must happen to pull the market out of hibernation."
Tatkov said Gazprom rose after prices for its shares rose slightly at a weekly auction. Traders had expected them to fall.
A stake of 10 million shares was sold at an average 2,901 roubles a share, up from 2,891 roubles a week ago.
Gazprom rose to $0.42 on the Russian Trading System from $0.40 at Wednesday's close.
But Tatkov said Gazprom would not rise any further due to a heavy inflow of cheap shares from the regions.

Ippolitov said Surgurneftegaz rose on the news that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission had given OAO Surgutneftegaz permission to proceed with an application to issue American Depositary Receipts.
"Russian brokers decided to buy some more Surgutneftegaz with free funds," he said.
Tatkov said LUKoil's first half year results issued on Thursday pushed prices up for a while, but the quotes fell soon on lack of Western support.
LUKoil said its output in the first six months of this year was 1.15 million barrels per day, 0.8 percent higher than a year earlier.
Rostelekom slipped to $2.55 from $2.56 and Norilsk Nickel fell to $7.70 from $7.75.
